## Rule

ARC-GEN generator `task_ff805c23.py` (`size=24`, `cutout=5`). The input is a
**dihedral-symmetric (D4) colored pattern** (the pattern uses black + 3 colors,
all ≠ blue) on a 24×24 grid with a **5×5 blue square occluding** part of it. The
output is the **reconstruction of the occluded 5×5 region** using the symmetry.
The generator's orbit-`shown` check + `while`-retry guarantee the hole is never
placed where it can't be reconstructed from a single h- or v-mirror.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
# blue == color 1 is the ONLY blue in the grid (pattern excludes blue)
y0 = first row containing blue;  x0 = first col containing blue   # hole top-left
hm = grid[23-(y0+r), x0+c   ]   # vertical-mirror window  (default)
vm = grid[y0+r,      23-(x0+c)]  # horizontal-mirror window (fallback)
out5x5 = vm if (hm window still contains blue) else hm           # pick hole-free mirror
output = pad(out5x5, top-left, 30x30)                            # encode answer grid
```

The canonical (cost 60,395) implements exactly this but in **F16 one-hot
[1,10,H,W]** throughout, so the cast (18,000), the 24×24 crop (11,520) and the
two full-canvas mirrors (11,520 each = 23,040) are all paid at 10× channel width
to produce a 5×5×10 = 250-value answer.

## Cost analysis

Canonical 60,395 dominators (measured, `inspect_task201.py`): Cast input→F16 [1,10,30,30]
**18,000** · 24×24 crop **11,520** · two full-canvas mirrors (hm row-flip + vm col-flip)
**11,520 each** · two [1,10,5,24] row-gathers 2,400 each. **The entire cost is the 10-channel
width** carried through a graph whose answer is only 5×5×10 = 250 values.

> NOTE: the prompt's lever ("a [1,10,30,30] INT64 = 72,000 dominates") was STALE recon — that
> INT64 is the generic `cost_floor_reference.md` "worst common bloat", not present in the
> current model. The real cost is the F16 one-hot intermediates above. Always re-measure.

**Fix = collapse the channel dim before the expensive ops.** A 1×1 Conv (weights `[0..9]`)
turns the one-hot into a single-channel color-index canvas [1,1,30,30] F32 = **3,600**; every
data intermediate then shrinks ~10× ([1,1,5,30]=600 vs [1,10,5,24]=2,400). The exact
anchor/mirror/select logic runs in canvas space; an `Equal(canvas, [0..9])` re-expands the
chosen 5×5 to one-hot at the very end (250+500 B). v2 sentinel trick (blue→100) folds the
anchor into the same canvas via `ReduceMax`, removing the separate 2,304-B ch1 slice.

**Floor (UPDATED 2026-06-01 — supersedes the earlier "5,730 floor / sub-3,000 impossible" claim, which was WRONG).**
The earlier analysis assumed the color canvas must be a full `[1,1,30,30]` F32 = 3,600 B. It is not: a
**dilated crop-collapse Conv** crops 30→24 AND collapses the 10 channels in ONE op (kernel `[1,10,2,2]`,
`dilations=[6,6]`, color-selector only on the `(0,0)` tap ⇒ `output[i,j]=color(input[i,j])`), giving a
`[1,1,24,24]` F32 canvas = **2,304 B** for 40 params. This drops the whole model to **v6b = 3,557**
(byte-/value-equal on 200k), a 17× reduction.

### scorer-VALID floor is now ~3,034 (core), ~3,550 (full model)

The official `calculate_memory` runs `infer_shapes(strict_mode=True)` and rejects any non-static dim,
so dynamic extraction must use **Gather** (static output = static index shape), not a dynamic Slice
(v5's `[unk,…]` → cost None, unsubmittable). The irreducible **core path**:
- **(1) grid colors** `[1,1,24,24]` F32 = **2,304** — the dilated crop-collapse. F32 is forced (Conv
  output dtype = input dtype); an F16 canvas (1,152) needs a Cast of the counted F32 output (→3,456) or
  a full-input F16 cast (18,000); a U8 canvas needs the F32 precursor too.
- **(2) dynamic 5×5 extract** first Gather `[1,1,5,24]` F32 = **480** (a static Gather reduces one axis
  to 5; the other stays 24; GatherND→[1,1,5,5] needs a ~600-B meshgrid index, net worse).
- **(3) one-hot expand** `Equal→[1,10,5,5]` BOOL = **250**.

**core = 2,304 + 480 + 250 = 3,034 B > 3,000**, before the anchor (2× ReduceMax = 192), index plumbing
(~120 INT32), and params (~68). So **a submittable sub-3,000 model appears impossible** — each core
item is at its dtype/shape floor. (Caveat: I was wrong once about the floor here; if a cheaper static
grid read or dynamic extractor exists, sub-3,000 opens up. None found across canvas / crop-collapse /
wide-conv / GatherND / fold-by-symmetry attempts.) **v6b (3,557) = lowest; v3 (5,730) = byte-equal ship.**

## Don't-do log

- **Don't trust the prompt's "72,000 INT64" lever** — stale. The current model has no
  [1,10,30,30] INT64; cost is F16 one-hot intermediates. Re-measure with `inspect_task201.py`.
- **Don't pursue the byte-exact Path-A reorder alone** (flip∘gather → gather∘flipped-idx,
  removing only hm/vm) — lands ~37,000; and **don't gather the one-hot from F32 input** (rows
  [1,10,5,30] F32 = 6,000 ×2) — lands ~17,000. The Conv channel-collapse beats both (~6,700).
- **Don't try to shrink the 3,600 canvas**: cropping the Conv output to 24×24 (Slice) keeps the
  3,600 intermediate AND adds the slice; F16/U8 canvas needs an 18,000/9,000 full-input cast;
  ArgMax-over-channels for a color index emits [1,1,30,30] INT64 = 7,200. All net-worse.
- **DO replace the 2-mirror select with the arithmetic decision** (v3): `use_vm = (8 ≤ y0 ≤ 11)`
  is **provably exact** ∀ y0∈[0,19] (the vertical-mirror window's columns always equal the hole's,
  so window-overlaps-hole ⟺ rows overlap ⟺ y0 centered). I initially feared this would diverge on
  center holes and forfeit byte-equality — **it does not**: v3 is byte_equal 200266/200266. It saves
  one full mirror gather (~700 B). Gather ONE mirror with `Where`-selected index lists.
- **The F16 output cast is optional, NOT mandatory** for the gate. v4 drops it (BOOL output) →
  5,230, and ng_gate ab still passes 200266/200266 because the gate uses `np.array_equal`
  (True/False ≡ 1.0/0.0, value-equal). BUT the BOOL output is NOT raw bit-identical to the F16
  canonical — keep the F16 cast (v3) for a true byte-identical ship unless the captain accepts the
  dtype change for the last 500 B / +0.09 LB.
- **Don't use a dynamic Slice (computed starts/ends) to shrink an extraction** — even if it runs and is
  byte-correct in ORT, `score_network_v2` returns **None** because `infer_shapes(strict_mode=True)`
  can't give the output a static shape. v5 (~2,500 B, byte-equal in ORT) is unsubmittable for this
  reason. Use **Gather** (static output shape = index shape) for any dynamic-index extraction.
- **DO use the DILATED crop-collapse** (v6/v6b): one `Conv` with kernel `[1,10,2,2]`, `dilations=[6,6]`,
  color-selector only on the `(0,0)` tap crops 30→24 AND collapses channels → `[1,1,24,24]` canvas
  (2,304 B, 40 params). Far cheaper than the `[1,1,30,30]` 1×1-conv canvas (3,600) OR a dense 7×7 crop
  (490 params). This was the breakthrough that beat the (wrong) earlier "5,730 floor": v6b = 3,557.
- **sub-3,000 is out of reach** (core path 2,304 + 480 + 250 = 3,034 > 3,000). The single-step-extract
  lever (replace the 480-B two-step row+col gather) was TESTED 2026-06-01 and FAILED both ways:
  (a) **GatherND** requires INT64 indices, so the `Expand`+`Concat` meshgrid `[1,1,5,5,2]` INT64 = ~880 B
  > the 480 it replaces → **v7 = 4,084 (worse)**; (b) **flat-Gather** on a reshaped `[1,1,576]` canvas:
  `Reshape` output IS counted by `calculate_memory` (probe: 2,304 canvas + 2,304 flat = 4,612), so it's a
  wash. The two-step gather (480) is the cheapest valid dynamic 5×5 extract. **v6b (3,557) is the floor —
  task400 RETIRED, no further work.** (SHIPPED: v6b +2.83 LB → 6404.30; BOOL output held on the grader.)
